newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall, further declines seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall, further declines seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 0.26 percent on Wednesday, pushed lower by a lack of customer interest and concerns that a new tax on trading profits would continue to weigh down the market.
Market participants predicted that shares would continue to slide until the end of the year.
The 10-share SBI index fell 3.03 points to 1,160.3, declining for the third consecutive day.
"We are happy that trading closed for today, because if it would continue like this, the outlook would be even more miserable," said Ljudmila Bajec, a trader at brokers Dolenjska.
Turnover fell to 240.4 million tolars from 735.3 million tolars. Overall nine shares fell, five rose and three were unchanged, while another eight were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 0.43 percent to 41,820 tolars on volume of 3,316 shares.
SKB last month announced plans to list its shares on the London Stock Exchange.
Financial consultancy Primofin led the day's decliners, falling 4.19 percent to 27,200 tolars on volume of 38 shares.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank were the biggest gainer, firming 10 percent to 11,550 tolars on volume of 200 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
